title: Government orders GitHub to remove Bluetooth-based chat app Bitchat: Jack Dorsey
titleZh: 政府命令 GitHub 删除基于蓝牙的聊天应用程序 Bitchat：Jack Dorsey
author: rootkea
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Bitchat app’s developer and former Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey shared a copy of the notice dated July 23, 2026, on the X platform. File. | Photo Credit: The Hindu The Home Ministry’s cybercrime arm, the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre, has ordered Microsoft subsidiary GitHub to remove Bluetooth-based messaging application Bitchat, according to a notice.“The Government of India does not like technologies like Bitchat and wants it taken down,” said the app’s developer and former Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey on Friday (July 24, 2026) in an X post, sharing a copy of the notice dated July 23.A query sent to I4C in this regard elicited no immediate reply.In its notice, I4C said that the app enables communication even during network restrictions and creates a substantial risk of misuse by anti-national elements, terrorist organisations, organised criminal groups and cyber criminals seeking to evade lawful detection and continue communication despite legally imposed restrictions.While giving reference to Bitchat, I4C said that the content hosted or published by the GitHub intermediary platform is prohibited by law or being used to commit an unlawful act. I4C said that it has identified multiple applications as communication platforms capable of establishing decentralised peer-to-peer messaging over Bluetooth mesh networks without relying on mobile networks, internet connectivity, or centralised servers.“The application enables anonymous communication without mandatory user registration, phone number verification, or centralised logging of communications. The technical architecture of the application significantly impedes lawful interception, attribution and investigation by law enforcement agencies,” the notice said.The notice comes after several users participating in a protest organised by the Cockroach Janata Party at Jantar Mantar were observed using Bluetooth-based messaging apps after the government imposed temporary restrictions on internet services around the protest site.According to I4C, since communications occur directly between nearby devices through a decentralised mesh network, the platform can be misused to evade lawful surveillance, facilitate anonymous coordination, and circumvent lawful restrictions imposed by competent authorities during situations involving public disorder, riots, terrorism, organised crime, or internet shutdowns.“Intelligence inputs indicate that such decentralised communication platforms are capable of being exploited for coordinating unlawful assemblies, violent protests, dissemination of misinformation, radicalisation, criminal conspiracies, and other activities prejudicial to the sovereignty and integrity of India, defence of India, security of the State, public order, and facilitating the commission of cognizable offences,” the notice said.It added that the absence of a centralised service provider also limits the ability of law enforcement agencies to obtain subscriber information, communication records, or timely assistance during investigations.“The application’s design, which enables communication even during network restrictions, creates a substantial risk of misuse by anti-national elements, terrorist organisations, organised criminal groups, and cybercriminals seeking to evade lawful detection and continue communication despite legally imposed restrictions,” the notice mentioned.In the notice to GitHub, I4C has mentioned that the app violates Sections 43, 84B and 84C of the IT Act and Section 61 read with 196 and 197. Published - July 24, 2026 05:05 pm IST

comments.author: viktorcode
comments.textRawHtml:
> the app enables communication even during network restrictions and creates a substantial risk of misuse by anti-national elements, terrorist organisations, organised criminal groups and cyber criminals seeking to evade lawful detection and continue communication despite legally imposed restrictions.

This mouthful boils down to exactly this: a form of communication not controlled by the government creates a risk for the country.

Sorry for pointing out the obvious, but if your country's safety depends on ability to block all forms of private person to person messages, your government has failed in one of its primary goals: providing safety for its citizens. They can blame Dorsey, Telegram, WhatsApp and what not, but it is their failure. Things will not change until people notice the obvious and vote out incompetent persons in power.
comments.textZhHtml:
> 该应用程序即使在网络限制期间也能进行通信，并造成反国家分子、恐怖组织、有组织犯罪集团和网络犯罪分子滥用的巨大风险，他们试图逃避合法检测并在法律施加的限制下继续通信。

这句话归结为：不受政府控制的通信形式给国家带来了风险。

抱歉指出了显而易见的事实，但如果您的国家的安全取决于以下能力：阻止所有形式的私人对个人信息，您的政府未能实现其主要目标之一：为其公民提供安全。他们可以责怪 Dorsey、Telegram、WhatsApp 等，但这是他们的失败。除非人们注意到显而易见的事情并投票罢免无能的当权者，否则事情不会改变。

children.author: adityaathalye
children.textRawHtml:
Hilariously (darkly), during the pandemic, the very same reason is why the very same administrators were hell-bent on forcing Bluetooth-always-on contact tracing on the whole country's smartphone-carrying population.

(edit: viz. that forcible peer-to-peer bluetooth networking works. One man's unrestricted mass-surveillance is another person's "terrorist activity". Oh how the turntables turn and turn.)
children.textZhHtml:
可笑（黑暗）的是，在大流行期间，同样的原因为什么同样的管理员不遗余力地强制对全国智能手机携带者进行蓝牙始终开启的接触者追踪。

（编辑：即强制点对点蓝牙网络有效。一个人不受限制的大规模监视是另一个人的“恐怖活动”。哦，转盘转啊转啊。）

children.author: KitN
children.textRawHtml: But that did save lives; I was able to know my family had Covid before the symptoms showed up. Happened with a lot of other people too.
children.textZhHtml: 但这确实挽救了生命；在症状出现之前，我就知道我的家人感染了新冠病毒。很多其他人也发生过这种情况。

children.author: aeternum
children.textRawHtml: Indeed, and it would have saved far more lives if leveraged the app to have hazmat crews come in a forcibly carry the infected to quarantine zones.
children.textZhHtml: 确实，如果利用该应用程序让危险品工作人员强行将感染者运送到隔离区，将会挽救更多的生命。

children.author: Henchman21
children.textRawHtml:
Can we perhaps agree the that the response to COVID, worldwide, was essentially shit. When faced with a true crisis, the People in Charge fucking lost their minds. It’s laid bare for all to see:

Our governments have failed us worldwide.

I don’t know what we can do with that information. Feels both useless and that we’re helpless to fix it.
children.textZhHtml:
我们是否可以同意这样的观点：世界范围内对新冠病毒的反应本质上是糟糕的。当真正的危机来临的时候，那些负责人就彻底失去了理智。已经公开给大家看：

我们的政府在全世界都让我们失望了。

我不知道我们能用这些信息做什么。感觉既无用又无助于解决它。

children.author: ChoGGi
children.textRawHtml:
Depends on the government.

We go by province, mine was basically keep your distance and wear a mask (yeah, that pretty much was non-existent), whereas another one was; you can enter a coffee shop, but you can't use the washroom, you can buy construction shoes (not boots) in-store, but regular shoes you had to order and pickup outside.

It felt odd while there (I was visiting a friend with health issues).

I'm happy we didn't go too nutso.
children.textZhHtml:
取决于政府。

我们按省份去，我的基本上是保持距离并戴口罩（是的，这几乎不存在），而另一个是；你可以进入咖啡店，但不能使用洗手间，你可以在店内购买建筑鞋（不是靴子），但普通鞋你必须在外面订购和取货。

在那里感觉很奇怪（我正在拜访一位有健康问题的朋友）。

我很高兴我们没有太过疯狂。

children.author: canadaduane
children.textRawHtml:
There are gradations to failure. And "our governments" and "us" also overlap.

I'm probably more on your side than it sounds based on this comment, but I find it frustrating to encounter learned helplessness dressed in profundity.
children.textZhHtml:
失败是有等级的。 “我们的政府”和“我们”也有重叠。

根据这个评论，我可能比听起来更站在你一边，但我发现遇到深刻的习得性无助是令人沮丧的。

children.author: aand16
children.textRawHtml:
Australia just used police to move "close contacts" into "internment camps". Any wrong move inside would get punished by a $5000 fine.

> Hayley Hodgson [...] was ordered to go to the facility after a friend of hers tested positive for the virus and she was identified as a “close contact” by the number plate on her scooter.

> spent 14 days at the Howard Springs mandatory Covid-19 quarantine facility

> "Police officers blocked my driveway. ’What’s going on, are you guys testing me for Covid? What’s happening?’ They said, ‘No, you’re getting taken away. And you have no choice. You’re going to Howard Springs. You either come with us now, and we’ll put you in the back of the divvy van. Or you can have a choice to get a Covid cab.’

> they were even threatening me that if I was to do this again, ‘We will extend your time in here.’”

> Ms Hodgson said she told police “I don’t consent to this”, and asked why she couldn’t “just self-isolate at home”. Police responded ‘We’ve just been told from higher up where to take you. And that’s all that there is,’”.

> She was told to pack her bags and that she would be released when she tested negative. During her two-week stay she was tested three times, and each time tested negative.

> The video includes footage filmed by Ms Hodgson during her stay as she argues with a police officer at the facility, who reprimands her for leaving her cabin without a mask and threatens her with a $5000 fine.

> “I’m gonna give you a warning, yeah?” he says to her as she sits on the balcony. “It’s an official warning that you have to stay on your balcony and obey the rules while you’re here.” When she argues with the officer that the rules don’t make sense, he replies that “it doesn’t have to make sense”. [...] “Highly infectious when all of us people are negative?” she asks. “So far. The risk is still very high,” he says.

> She said at one point when she was distressed and asking to be let out of her room to go for a walk or a run, facility staff instead offered her Valium to calm down.

> Ms Hodgson said as a result of her two-week stay she had lost her casual retail job. “They compensated me $1500 for the two weeks, and that was all,” she said. “Now I’m currently unemployed because of this situation”

Full interview with recordings from inside the Australian "internment camp" https://unherd.com/newsroom/inside-australias-covid-internme...

Mirror: https://archive.ph/GQDkN
children.textZhHtml:
澳大利亚刚刚动用警察将“密切接触者”转移到“拘留营”。任何错误的举动都会被处以 5000 美元的罚款。

> 海莉·霍奇森 (Hayley Hodgson) [...] 在她的一位朋友的病毒检测呈阳性后被命令前往该机构，并通过她摩托车上的车牌将她识别为“密切接触者”。

> 在 Howard Springs 强制 Covid-19 隔离设施中度过了 14 天

> “警察封锁了我的车道。‘怎么了，你们在对我进行新冠病毒检测吗？发生了什么事？’他们说，‘不，你会被带走。你别无选择。你要去霍华德斯普林斯。你要么现在和我们一起走，我们会把你放在警车后面。或者你可以选择乘坐新冠出租车。’

> 他们甚至威胁我，如果我再这样做，‘我们将延长你在这里的时间。’”

> 霍奇森女士说，她告诉警方“我不同意这样做”，并询问为什么她不能“在家自我隔离”。警方回应说：“我们刚刚接到上级的通知，要带你去哪里。”这就是全部，’”。

> 她被告知收拾行李，待检测呈阴性后即可出院。在她逗留的两周内，她接受了三次检测，每次检测均为阴性。

> 该视频包括霍奇森女士在住宿期间与一名警察发生争执时拍摄的片段，警察斥责她不戴口罩离开小屋，并威胁要罚款 5000 美元。

> “我要警告你，好吗？”当她坐在阳台上时，他对她说道。 “这是官方警告，你在这里时必须呆在阳台上并遵守规则。”当她与警官争论这些规则没有意义时，他回答说“这不一定有意义”。 [...]“当我们所有人都是阴性时，传染性很强吗？”她问。 “到目前为止，风险仍然很高，”他说。

> 她说，有一次，当她感到痛苦并要求让她离开房间去散步或跑步时，设施工作人员反而给她提供了安定来让她平静下来。

> 霍奇森女士表示，由于停留两周，她失去了休闲零售工作。 “他们两周补偿了我 1500 美元，仅此而已，”她说。 “现在我因为这种情况失业了”

children.author: no_carrier
children.textRawHtml:
None of your three examples provide any evidence of hazmat crews forcibly taking away infected people. In fact, your links have absolutely nothing to do with anything at all. It's reasonable to assume that police would arrest people breaching curfew orders.

Under no circumstances was anyone in Australia forcibly removed by people in hazmat suits.
children.textZhHtml:
你的三个例子都没有提供任何危险品工作人员强行带走感染者的证据。事实上，您的链接绝对与任何事情无关。 可以合理地假设警察会逮捕违反宵禁令的人。

在澳大利亚，任何情况下都不会有人被身穿防护服的人强行带走。

children.author: no_carrier
children.textRawHtml: That's someone getting deported and has nothing to do with the claims that people were being forcibly removed into quarantine zones. This just didn't happen.
children.textZhHtml: 这是有人被驱逐出境，与人们被强行转移到隔离区的说法无关。但这并没有发生。

children.author: perpetuallunch
children.textRawHtml:
Your argument seems to boil down to a No True Hazmat Suit fallacy.

Where if the uniform worn isn’t quite right, and the location isn’t quite the same, and the presence or absence of one arbitrary infectious agent doesn’t match the criteria, then Everything Is Okay™.
children.textZhHtml:
您的论点似乎可以归结为“没有真正的危险品套装”的谬论。

如果穿着的制服不太合适，地点也不完全相同，并且是否存在任意一种传染性病原体不符合标准，那么一切都很好™。

children.author: cutterl6
children.textRawHtml: I doubt it, unless their hazmat suits are bullet-proof.
children.textZhHtml: 我对此表示怀疑，除非他们的防护服是防弹的。

children.author: aeternum
children.textRawHtml: Agreed, and I'm happy to live in a country where this is likely true.  The only thing more deadly than pandemics are governments that gained sufficient power to round up their citizens systematically in the name of the public good.
children.textZhHtml: 同意，我很高兴生活在一个可能是这样的国家。  唯一比流行病更致命的是政府获得了足够的权力以公共利益的名义系统地围捕其公民。
